blocks.c: "Ninety-nine year lease signed in 1874. Renewable at fifty-one year intervals, which is a stupid number, which is how you know a lawyer wrote it." Wen was moving now, pulling files. "1925. 1974. And today."

"The account settles. Every held dispute is determined by default in favour of the landlord unless heard. Every box out there is opened. And the caretaker's term ends and a new caretaker takes it on."
"I'm out at dawn either way. That's not the part that matters." She dumped a bundle of paper in front of me. "This is the part that matters."
It was the 1974 renewal. Signed. And the signature at the bottom, in a hand I had seen four hundred times on requisition forms and holiday rosters, was not from 1974.

"She signed as witness in 2003, retroactively, because the 1974 renewal was defective and it spent twenty-nine years looking for somebody to fix it." Wen's mouth was a line. "She thinks she has kept out of it by never getting in the elevator. She has been a party to this since her second week and she does not know it, and at dawn she is going to be the outgoing party to a lease renewal, and the outgoing party's account settles too."
I thought about a woman in a cardigan writing a name in her diary every morning so she would keep having it.
"Go and read it," she said. "It's the tall one at the end. And Ravi — walk. Don't run. It watches how fast you go towards things."
